\[
\begin{gathered}
G_x = P_x \star I, \quad G_y = P_y \star I,
\qquad
P_x = \begin{bmatrix} -1 & 0 & 1 \\ -1 & 0 & 1 \\ -1 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix},
\quad
P_y = P_x^{\mathsf T}
\end{gathered}
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(P_x, P_y\): The Prewitt kernels
- \(\star\): Correlation, without flipping

P_x takes a difference across the edge and a plain sum of three rows along it. P_y is the same turned by 90 degrees. The magnitude and direction combine G_x and G_y as for the Sobel filter. Compared with Sobel, the plain sum smooths less and treats the three rows equally.
